verdict.headline: September rate hike is the base case; Friday's payrolls will seal it or force a rethink
verdict.label: Step aside: Sep hike ~67%; Canada $19.9B tariffs Sep 8; NFP Sep 4 est. +475K; BTC $78.1K holds $76.6K support; 30Y at 5.20%, 10bps from trigger
verdict.horizon: Through September 4 NFP; posture reset after September 16 FOMC
verdict.rationale_short: Equity markets emerge from the weekend with no new session to reprice. The macro backdrop is unchanged from Friday's close: Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole delivery remains the dominant rate narrative, with September 16 FOMC hike probability holding near 67%. The one meaningful weekend development is BTC: the coin recovered from Saturday's intraday low of $76,864 — which tested the structural support named in the prior setup — to $78,151 Sunday morning (+0.67%), with the $76,661 Aug 24 support intact. A Sunday close above $78K going into Monday would be constructive but does not change the headline posture: BTC needs two consecutive daily closes above $80K to flip the near-term read bullish. The week ahead is the highest-density event corridor since the Jackson Hole run: ISM Manufacturing (Mon), ADP (Wed), Bank of Canada decision (Wed, expected hold), ISM Services (Thu), then NFP (Fri Sep 4, consensus +475K, unemployment 5.1%). Canada's retaliatory tariffs — $19.9B of US goods at 15%, 25%, and 50% rates — take effect September 8, just four days after NFP. A hot jobs print followed immediately by a tariff-stacking inflation impulse is the pathway to 30Y piercing the 5.30% regime trigger and the September hike becoming a near-certainty. INTU's 'AI competition' warning is entering its second week without a management walk-back; Monday's tape will reveal whether the SaaS read-across (ADSK, HUBS, DOCN) expands or the sell is absorbed as idiosyncratic. NVDA's Friday -4.3% sell-the-news reversal leaves the stock at ~$217, structurally below the $220 support — Monday's open will price whether this is a one-session reset or a deeper repricing cycle. Step aside posture intact through at minimum NFP Friday.

watchlist_mentions.note: Friday September 4, 8:30 AM ET: consensus +475K, unemployment 5.1%. This is the last major labor market data point before the September 16 FOMC. A print above 400K confirms the September hike is near-certain and likely pushes the 30Y toward the 5.30% trigger; below 200K would meaningfully reduce hike probability and could flip regime bias dovish. Given that Warsh's hawkish framing relied explicitly on inflation persistence through a strong labor market, Friday's number is the single most consequential event of the next 30 days. ADP on Wednesday (consensus: ~400K private payrolls) will serve as the directional signal-ahead.

$78,151 Sunday morning (+0.67% from yesterday's $77,635 open). Saturday's intraday low of $76,864 tested but held the $76,661 Aug 24 structural support — the named invalidation level from the prior setup. Sunday trading band: $77,499-$78,338. The Bessent buyback program starts September 9 (10 days), providing a structural demand backstop. Two consecutive daily closes above $80K remains the bull re-entry criterion. A Monday open above $78.5K on risk-on tape would be constructive but does not yet satisfy that criterion.

~$217 (estimated Sunday; Thursday post-earnings close ~$226.15, Friday close estimated $216-218 down ~4.3%). The full sell-the-news reversal of the Thursday +6% earnings pop is the fourth instance of the high-multiple AI infrastructure repricing pattern (CSCO, AMAT, MRVL, NVDA). $220 structural support is the critical level; a Monday open and close below $220 opens the $210 gap fill. Next Blackwell production data point expected around AVGO earnings (estimated September 4-5). The Friday reversal, while negative, is not a new catalyst — it was priced Friday. Monday is the first session where dip-buyers and sellers resolve the distribution question.

~$395-400 (Friday close, -9.2%). The 'AI competition' demand erosion narrative has had two days to age — no management walk-back, no analyst upgrade. JPMorgan PT $331 remains the downside anchor with a fresh downgrade. Monday's session will reveal whether the SaaS read-across expands (ADSK, HUBS, DOCN selling sympathetically) or whether the market treats INTU as idiosyncratic. A 3-5% bounce toward $415-420 on low volume is the short re-entry signal per the prior setup; a recovery above $430 would signal the sell was overdone.

~$263-265 (Friday close, +3.06% post-earnings). The Salesforce/Intuit AI software fault line is now the defining sector bifurcation: AI-as-product (CRM, ServiceNow) vs. AI-as-substitute (INTU, legacy workflow SaaS). Monday's tape will test whether CRM holds the post-earnings premium on risk-off broadmarket tape or whether the macro backdrop overwhelms company-specific strength. CRM holding above $260 is the confirmation that the bifurcation read-through has legs.

~$460 (estimated Sunday; +9% Thursday post-earnings). Monday is the first full post-earnings absorptive session. Cybersecurity's structural insulation from AI substitution risk — AI expands the threat surface, increasing CRWD TAM — remains the bull thesis. A Monday close above $460 on normal volume signals post-earnings base is holding; a close below $445 would signal distribution.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y yield — five-day gauntlet with 10bps of headroom to regime trigger
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y enters the week at 5.20%, 10bps from the 5.30% regime trigger. The week-ahead event stack — ADP Wednesday, NFP Friday (+475K consensus), Canada tariffs September 8 — is the most concentrated inflation/rate catalyst corridor since Jackson Hole. A hot NFP print (above 400K) combined with Canada tariff repricing of import prices could push 30Y above 5.30% by Monday of the following week. Warsh's three-dissenter hawkish bloc makes a rate hike at the September 16 FOMC the base case; a formal 30Y trigger breach this week would be the first time the regime framework activates since its construction.
trade_setups.entry: Daily close above 5.30% on 30Y formally activates the regime framework and converts the step-aside posture to bearish. Inverse: 30Y closes at or below 5.10% after a soft NFP (sub-200K) would signal the trigger is deactivating through the September FOMC window.
trade_setups.invalidation: NFP September 4 prints below 200K and 30Y closes at or below 5.10% on September 4.
trade_setups.horizon: Through September 4 NFP; hard posture reset on September 16 FOMC outcome.

trade_setups.asset: BTC — $76,661 support held; Bessent bid T-minus 10 days
trade_setups.thesis: BTC's Saturday intraday low ($76,864) tested and held the $76,661 Aug 24 structural support. Sunday recovery to $78,151 shows the support level has held over the weekend. With the Bessent buyback program starting September 9, there is a defined structural demand backstop approaching in 10 days. The trade: hold above $76,661 through Monday's open; two consecutive closes above $80K is the bull confirmation. A Monday close below $76,661 is the exit signal — confirmed failed breakout, next support is the $72-73K prior range top.
trade_setups.entry: Hold long above $76,661 with the Bessent bid as structural lower bound. Re-enter aggressively on two consecutive daily closes above $80K.

trade_setups.asset: INTU / IGV SaaS AI repricing — monitoring read-across on Monday open
trade_setups.thesis: INTU's Friday close at ~$395-400 established the AI substitution repricing baseline. Monday is the first session where the read-across either confirms (ADSK, HUBS, DOCN selling) or denies (INTU idiosyncratic, sector stabilizes) the broader SaaS de-rating thesis. A 3-5% sector bounce into resistance is the short entry on AI-as-substitute exposure.
trade_setups.entry: Short IGV or individual names (ADSK, HUBS, DOCN) on a 3-5% bounce from Friday close, targeting relative weakness vs. S&P. Monday open on risk-on tape is the entry window.
trade_setups.invalidation: INTU recovers above $430 on volume; IGV holds its 20-day moving average on the first session.
trade_setups.horizon: 3-5 sessions through first week of September.

bear_case: The bear case has a specific pathway and a five-day fuse. If NFP September 4 prints above 400K (consensus +475K), the September 16 rate hike is near-certain. Canada's retaliatory tariffs ($19.9B, 15-50% rates) take effect four days later on September 8, injecting a tariff-stacking inflation impulse into the same week a hot labor market is cementing the hike thesis. The 30Y, already at 5.20% (10bps from trigger), would be expected to breach 5.30% in this scenario — formally activating the regime framework for the first time. NVDA at $217 is already in a technical failure pattern; a Monday open below $210 would signal the AI infrastructure repricing is expanding beyond one-session distribution. INTU's 'AI competition' language has not been walked back — if Monday brings sympathetic selling in ADSK, HUBS, or DOCN, the SaaS sector faces a multiple compression event that runs independent of the rate backdrop. The combined scenario — rate hike locked in + tariff inflation stacking + AI-substitute repricing across software — is the bear case for SPX 7,500-7,600 by September 16 FOMC. Conversion from step-aside to outright bearish requires a close below SPX 7,600 post-NFP or a 30Y close above 5.30% on any session this week.
